title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous pages): S is a scheme over T (or a topos), and E is an O_S-module with an integrable connection, written either as δ_E or as the first differential d^0_E of the de Rham complex E⊗Ω•_{S/T}. De Rham cohomology is defined as hypercohomology, H^*_DR(S,E) = H^*(S, E⊗Ω•). Truncating the complex to its degree-0 term, E⊗Ω• → E, gives a comparison map (14) H^i_DR(S,E) → H^i(S,E). This page studies (14) for i = 0 and i = 1.

(1) i = 0. H^0_DR(S,E) is the group of horizontal sections, those x with d^0_E x = 0. In the language of connections as identifications of the two pullbacks of E to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood, this says δ_E x = d^1_E x. So (14) for i = 0 is just the inclusion of horizontal sections into all global sections Γ(S,E).

(2) i = 1. This is a general topos-theoretic lemma. Let K• : 0 → K^0 → K^1 → K^2 → ... be a complex of abelian sheaves on a topos S. Then H^1(S,K•) is the group of isomorphism classes of a category C(K•). Its objects are pairs (P, ξ):
- P is a K^0-torsor;
- ξ is a section of the pushed-out K^1-torsor P^1 = P ×^{K^0} K^1;
- the image d^1_*(ξ) in P^2 = P ×^{K^0} K^2 ≅ P^1 ×^{K^1} K^2 must equal the canonical trivialisation. That trivialisation exists because d^1 d^0 = 0, so P^2 is canonically trivial.
The morphisms are left implicit ('on devine'). The construction is covariant in K•. Under it, the map H^1(S,K•) → H^1(S,K^0) induced by the truncation K• → K^0 corresponds to the forgetful functor (P, ξ) ↦ P.

The page then begins to reformulate ξ. Given P, a trivialisation ξ of P^1 is the same as an isomorphism P^1 ≅ K^1. The next page finishes the thought: ξ amounts to a map d̄^0 : P → K^1 with d̄^0(x f) = d̄^0(x) + d^0 f, i.e. a d^0-affine map, and the cocycle condition says d̄^0 lands in Z^1 = Ker d^1.

Applied to K• = E⊗Ω•, this gives the familiar classification: H^1_DR(S,E) classifies E-torsors equipped with an integrable connection compatible with ∇_E. The map to H^1(S,E) forgets the connection. In modern terms this is the standard description of H^1 of a complex, which depends only on the two-term complex K^0 → Z^1(K), as torsors under that complex (equivalently under the associated Picard stack). It is the groundwork for describing the kernel and image of H^1_DR → H^1, i.e. the obstruction to the existence of connections on torsors. The NB on the next page notes that connections on P form a torsor under E⊗Ω^1.
errors: The equation for horizontality is labelled (16) in the manuscript, not (15); (15) was already used on the previous page for the truncation map.
'triples (P,ξ)' is a slip: the objects are pairs (P, ξ).

Morphisms of C(K•) are not specified ('on devine'), and no proof is given that iso classes form H^1. The claim is nonetheless correct (standard via Čech hypercocycles or the two-term complex K^0 → Z^1).
The group law on iso classes (contracted product of torsors with sum of trivialisations) is not stated. This is minor.

ideas.what: H^0_DR(S,E) equals horizontal sections, and H^0_DR → H^0 is the inclusion
ideas.where_published: standard; cf. Katz 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970), Deligne LNM 163

ideas.what: H^1 of a complex of abelian sheaves on a topos classifies K^0-torsors P with a trivialisation of P×^{K^0}K^1 compatible with d^1
ideas.modern_name: torsors under a two-term complex / Picard stack; H^1 of the complex K^0 → Z^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (SGA 4 XVIII §1.4, Picard stacks and two-term complexes, 1973); Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971)

ideas.what: H^1_DR(S,E) classifies E-torsors with an integrable connection compatible with that of E; the map to H^1(S,E) forgets the connection
ideas.modern_name: torsors with flat connection; extensions with connection; one-dimensional de Rham/crystalline cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur–Messing (LNM 370, 1974); also standard in Deligne's Hodge theory and later Breen–Messing
ideas.where_published: Mazur–Messing, 'Universal extensions and one-dimensional crystalline cohomology' (1974)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard reformulation of the low-degree comparison H^i_DR → H^i in terms of torsors with connection. Equivalent statements appear in Deligne (SGA 4 XVIII), Giraud and Mazur–Messing. Nothing appears new.
transcription_corrections: Equation number on the horizontality line reads '(16)', not '(15)'.
Margin note reads approximately 'Comparer cat. cf. additionnelle 1.8' rather than 'cf. Lie cat. cf. additionnelle 1.8'.
